title: Global Spherical Shells on Minimal Surfaces of Class VII
main_claim: The paper claims to prove the Global Spherical Shell conjecture: every minimal compact complex surface with b1=1, kappa=-infinity and b2>0 contains a global spherical shell. If there is no square-zero divisor (that case is Enoki's theorem), the proof builds compact classes e on the infinite cyclic cover with e^2=K.e<0. Weighted Dolbeault index theory gives each one a holomorphic section that tends to 1 at the positive end and to 0 at the negative end. Every component of its divisor is then shown to be compact and rational. A Laurent-polynomial count then forces at least b2 rational curves, so Dloussky-Oeljeklaus-Toma applies.

issues.location: sections/weighted.tex, Lemma weighted:continuation (scalar case near z=0)
issues.description: The meromorphic continuation through the trivial character uses the functional ell. The paper only says ell is obtained 'by pairing with the harmonic representative' and does not say in which Sobolev scale. It also asserts without proof that the residue is constant. Both are standard and fixable, and the Remark that follows checks the second one independently, so this is not a gap in the argument.
issues.evidence: "Choose a continuous scalar functional ell on degree-one forms which annihilates im d and for which ell(A1)!=0 ... The residue is a constant, since the pole part in the differential equation is annihilated by d."

coverage: I read the whole LaTeX source: paper.tex and every section (surfaces, compact-data, weighted, curves, cylinder, conclusion). I checked these steps in detail. (1) The class VII reductions and the Donaldson-diagonalisation argument giving K=sum u_i. (2) Character acyclicity. (3) The Gauduchon height with Lh=c>0 (the primitive anti-self-dual argument). (4) The seam-torsion grouping, which loses only C0=sum(k_tau-1) classes independent of n, and e^2=K.e=-m. (5) The Fredholm/Fourier-Laplace setup. (6) The weighted duality. (7) The positive-tail nondecay barrier, with signs checked. (8) The base index 1 at weights (a,b)>0 and the compact excision with Riemann-Roch, giving index 1+(e^2-K.e)/2. (9) The argument that c_-=0, via the projection formula and K.D>=0. (10) The exponential area bound from three-circle propagation. (11) Degree-one vanishing at weights (-eps,b), using index constancy from the acyclic pair (-b,b). (12) The residue/support argument (normal-jet expansion). (13) Genus zero via L^2 harmonic forms and Koebe. (14) The small-energy Bishop compactness argument. (15) The flat-chain Fourier contraction (2/(e^P-1)), the charging and counting in the cylinder estimate, and the periodic gauge with Trudinger. (16) The plane-case decay |H|<=C/|z| that cancels dz=e^v dv. (17) The Laurent pairing count with q<=nr<d, and the curve-class independence upper bound. I also did a sanity check on a b2=1 model with a nodal curve: the lifted chain has C_k^2=-3, and the recursion a_{m-1}-3a_m+a_{m+1}=0 gives a bounded-above infinite effective divisor with exponentially growing multiplicities. This matches the paper's structure, including the area exponent A. I did not check the cited external theorems (Enoki, DOT2003, Kato, Bishop/Harvey-Shiffman, Albanese-Di Cerbo-Lombardi) beyond their quoted statements, and I did not verify every Sobolev constant.
